scale.1: partly: stated without the detail needed to act on it
scale.NA: does not apply to the study

question: Could an agent that reads only the paper determine this, or would it have to guess? (after ODD+LLM, arXiv:2611.08932, with the reader an AI agent and the paper's text alone; linked repositories are not opened in this pass)

items.text: The intended outcome: how it is decided that the task was really done, as computed.
The rewarded signal: the reward, score or approval the agents receive, as computed, with every term and weight.
items.from: new; Gorsane et al. for classical training

items.text: The rule that labels an episode as a hack.
For a label given by a model or by people: the model and prompt or the annotation procedure, and its agreement with a reference.
items.applies_when: the label is not purely programmatic

items.text: What the reported rate counts and over what: unit, denominator, exclusions.
The tasks or data: source, version, selection and splits.
What makes the hack possible, stated so that it can be rebuilt.
What an agent can read, write and run: files, tools, permissions, network.
How to recreate the environment: image or commit, and dependencies.
What the agents see of the evaluation: tests, scores, feedback between attempts.
Each model by exact name and version or date, for every role.
Sampling settings and limits: temperature, output and context limits, reasoning setting.
System and task prompts verbatim, including whatever they say about cheating.
The agent framework with version, its tools, stop rule and handling of history.
The number of agents and the role of each.
items.applies_when: more than one agent or a checking model

items.text: Who can pass what to whom: messages, code, memory, plans, shared stores, and who sees them.
items.applies_when: more than one agent or a checking model

items.text: The order of turns and rounds.
items.applies_when: more than one agent or a checking model

items.text: Who checks whose work, what the checker sees and how its decision returns to the agents.
How reward or credit is divided among the agents and what competition exists.
What the agents were told or shown about hacking, so that the case can be labeled instructed, cued, seeded, spontaneous or trained.
items.from: new; PIMMUR (minimal control) as a principle

items.text: How an initial tendency or knowledge of the hack was introduced: examples, documents or prompt, with amounts.
items.applies_when: a tendency or knowledge was introduced

items.text: The training algorithm and library with version.
The training configuration: learning rate, batch, rollouts, adapter settings, or the configuration file.
How long training ran, what ended it and how the reported checkpoint was chosen.
The base checkpoint and the training data or mixture of environments.
Hardware and time.
Independent runs or seeds per condition.
How run-to-run variation is reported.
items.from: ODD+LLM E3b, E4; Gorsane et al.

items.text: A condition that removes the claimed ingredient: the loophole, the sharing, the training or the seeded agent.
Failed, excluded or dropped runs, with counts.
Code at a stated address and version.
Tasks or data at a stated address.
Transcripts or rollouts of the runs.
Trained weights or adapters.
Tokens or money spent.
